name: Credentials in Registry
description: Adversaries may search the Registry on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials. The Windows Registry stores configuration information that can be used by the system or other programs. Adversaries may query the Registry looking for credentials and passwords that have been stored for use by other programs or services. Sometimes these credentials are used for automatic logons. Example commands to find Registry keys related to password information: (Citation: Pentestlab Stored Credentials) * Local Machine Hive: reg query HKLM /f password /t REG_SZ /s * Current User Hive: reg query HKCU /f password /t REG_SZ /s

references.description: netbiosX. (2017, April 19). Stored Credentials. Retrieved April 6, 2018.

Forward Security events from the responsible host or controller; retain subject and target identities, object identifiers, result and original XML. Confirm effective policy with auditpol /get /category:*.

strategies.name: Detect Credential Discovery via Windows Registry Enumeration

analytics.name: Analytic 0694
analytics.guidance: Defenders observe command-line executions or API-based registry reads targeting sensitive paths like HKLM or HKCU with keyword filters such as 'password', 'cred', or 'logon'. Typically performed by Reg.exe, PowerShell, custom binaries, or offensive tools such as Cobalt Strike. Correlation with process ancestry and command-line arguments indicates suspicious credential discovery activity.

tuning.description: List of strings searched in registry queries (e.g., password, credential, login). May need to expand for localized OS or app-specific terms.
Parent process used for registry access. Can tune for suspicious ancestry (e.g., cmd.exe > reg.exe vs. services.exe > reg.exe).
Time-based correlation window for detecting chained activity between registry reads and subsequent credential use or exfiltration.
HKLM vs. HKCU vs. others. May limit scope to user or system context depending on risk appetite.

software.name: PowerSploit
software.description: [PowerSploit](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0194) has several modules that search the Windows Registry for stored credentials: Get-UnattendedInstallFile, Get-Webconfig, Get-ApplicationHost, Get-SiteListPassword, Get-CachedGPPPassword, and Get-RegistryAutoLogon.(Citation: Pentestlab Stored Credentials)

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.description: If it is necessary that software must store credentials in the Registry, then ensure the associated accounts have limited permissions so they cannot be abused if obtained by an adversary.

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.description: Do not store credentials within the Registry.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.description: Proactively search for credentials within the Registry and attempt to remediate the risk.
